proof_results: Unweighted: bounded coefficientwise convergence to a bounded sequence implies actual WeakDual(Coeff 1) convergence for arbitrary filters.
Unweighted: weak-star convergence implies every coefficient converges; hence equivalence on bounded families.
Weighted: for every real s, bounded coefficientwise convergence implies WeakDual(WeightedCoeff (sobolev (-s)) 1) convergence with physical index reversal.
Weighted: finite truncations converge weak-star at infinity for every real s.
Original periodic distributions: bounded modewise convergence implies actual Wiener-predual weak-star convergence via existing pseudomeasureDualIsometry.
All real predual orders r: entire weighted endpoint norm balls are weak-star compact, metrizable and sequentially compact. Parameter r denotes predual order; source coefficient order is s=-r.
Every bounded subset has exactly its coordinate-induced topology, expressed as an actual topological embedding; criterion holds for arbitrary filters.
Arbitrary sets in this weak dual are compact iff sequentially compact iff norm-bounded and weak-star closed; sequential compactness implies boundedness by Banach-Steinhaus.
Weak-star convergence of sequences is equivalent to boundedness plus coefficient convergence; boundedness is derived in the forward direction.
For every finite ENNReal exponent p with Fact(1<=p), at (-r-t)*p.toReal>1, the lower norm realization preserves raw coefficients and induces exactly the weak-star topology on bounded sets.
Weak-star sequence convergence is equivalent to boundedness plus lower weighted norm convergence at every admissible pair (t,p).
A set is weak-star compact iff norm bounded and its actual lower weighted norm image is compact.
Real conjugate-symmetric mean-zero coefficients form a closed subset; its intersections with weighted norm balls are compact, metrizable and sequentially compact.
Reusable endpoint results moved to shared NLS/SequenceSpaces and NLS/Fourier modules, preserving existing article import paths.
Existing ActionDependentWeightedPhaseFlow reused byte-for-byte from c794d144d9e58aa28e05833c4338bb050df607ef on articles/kdv-kdv2-frequencies; its 14 declarations are included in the fresh audit.
For arbitrary real frequencies depending on squared amplitudes, the weighted endpoint flow has the group law and exactly preserves its strong dual norm at every time.
Every endpoint orbit is weak-star continuous without a continuity hypothesis on the frequency functional.
On bounded input families, coordinatewise continuous realized frequencies give joint weak-star continuity and continuous dependence in the compact-open compact-time trajectory space.
For bounded invariant subsets, continuous dependence is proved with codomain C([-T,T],V), retaining the weak-star subtype topology. Odd frequencies preserve the real mean-zero locus.

Existing PeriodicSobolevDuality transports to a proved coefficientWeakDualHomeomorph. Weighted original-distribution norm balls are compact in the actual original Wiener weak dual; smooth-test evaluation is exactly the original normalized distribution action.
The compact-open trajectory topology is induced by the lower realization on all bounded subsets. Article specialization gives the H^-1 coefficient trajectory topology exactly for s>-1/2.
For arbitrary period-two tempered distributions, physical period one is equivalent to vanishing of all odd normalized Fourier coefficients; no lp or measure hypothesis is used.
Reality on all original smooth tests, zero mean and physical period one are exactly the signed-real, zero-mode and even-mode coefficient conditions.

Potential(r), with data order s=-r, is an actual original-distribution subtype. Its bijection to the constrained coefficient weak dual preserves the exact norm. Its coordinate norm balls are closed, compact, metrizable and sequentially compact.
RealWienerTest(r) is bijective and norm preserving with the entire original real mean-zero physically one-periodic Wiener space. The proof is not restricted to finite tests.
The physical action of source potentials on real Wiener tests is real valued, so the real-part evaluation used for sigma topology loses no information.

On every norm-bounded source subset, actual original real-Wiener test evaluations form a topological embedding. This proves the exact real-predual weak-star topology and arbitrary-filter convergence criterion on the bounded sets needed by main Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4.
At 0<=r<1/2, the original source potential embeds into original H^-1 as literally the same smooth-test distribution; all physical source restrictions and normalization are unchanged.
Mixed reciprocal Hill lattice sum has explicit bound (4+8/a)*n^(-a/2) for every 0<a<=1; summability and the bound are proved without a finite source exponent.
For every source spectral weight w and negative Sobolev order s=-r with 0<=r<1/2, the shifted convolution weight ratio is bounded by exactly one squared positive Sobolev factor, independently of w.
The normalized weighted-infinity rows define a continuous linear operator. The original Fourier rows are absolutely convergent and equal sum_k q_(m-k)*reducedHillSymbol(k)*f_k.
Both +n and -n shifted norms satisfy the operator bound C_s*n^(-(1/2-|s|))*norm(q), with C_s=8+16/(1+2s). C_s>=1 and is antitone in s.

Coefficient-preserving continuous shift equivalences transport both realizations to the same operator on the original unshifted source Banach space. Its two shifted norms satisfy the literal source bound.
For every regularity and potential norm bound, a single cutoff precedes every weight, potential, mode and lambda and makes both shifted operators half contractions.
The actual endpoint tail equations have two-sided continuous linear inverses of norm at most two; eventual invertibility of both shifted operators follows uniformly on each potential norm ball.
